md_description: This workflow covers the study of medicinal plants to uncover biosynthetic pathways for alkaloid production. It includes plant sampling, DNA preparation and genome sequencing, computational identification and annotation of biosynthetic gene clusters, metabolite extraction, and chemical characterization of alkaloids. The resulting genomic and chemical data are integrated to relate gene clusters and pathway genes to medically important alkaloid products.

selected_medicinal_plants.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic identity/origin fields for the selected plant species and excluded any process, capture, signal, or derivative details. Because this is the root biological source in the DAG, the key metadata are the plant taxon identity and collection/origin context that define what the studied organisms are. I avoided sampling, extraction, sequencing, metabolomics, or annotation fields because those belong to downstream process/capture nodes. I also avoided repeating any experiment/sample identifiers that could be generated elsewhere, and kept the schema minimal to stay within the entity territory of this node.

md_schema.descr: Accepted botanical taxon name for each selected medicinal plant species studied as the alkaloid source; use standard binomial or trinomial nomenclature, for example 'Catharanthus roseus' or 'Papaver somniferum subsp. setigerum'. This is recorded at the plant-selection stage before any sampling or processing.

Common or vernacular name used by the study team for the selected medicinal plant species, for example 'Madagascar periwinkle' or 'opium poppy'. Record at selection/curation time to aid traceability of the biological source.

Taxonomic resolution at which the plant source is designated in the study; use this to indicate whether the selected organism is identified at species, subspecies, or cultivar level. Recorded during plant selection, prior to sampling.

Botanical family assigned to the selected medicinal plant species, recorded from taxonomic curation of the source organism, for example 'Apocynaceae' or 'Papaveraceae'. This describes the biological identity of the plant, not the sampling procedure.

Natural or cultivated origin of the selected plant source, such as country, region, or locality where the specimen population is native, cultivated, or collected. Record at selection time to capture biological provenance relevant to alkaloid diversity.

Herbarium or voucher identifier assigned to the selected plant specimen, in string form such as 'HSC-2024-015' or a herbarium accession code. This is the persistent source identifier for the biological material and is recorded at selection/curation stage.

Brief note on why the plant was selected for alkaloid pathway study, such as known production of medically important alkaloids or prior evidence of biosynthetic gene clusters. Record as a curation attribute of the source organism, not as an experimental result.

Conservation or legal status of the selected plant source, if tracked in the study, for example 'not_evaluated', 'least_concern', 'vulnerable', or 'protected'. This is an intrinsic/curated property of the organism at selection time.

plant_sampling.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only fields that describe how plant tissue collection and partitioning were performed, plus a basic process-quality outcome. I excluded entity fields about the plant itself because those belong to the upstream selected_medicinal_plants node, and I excluded downstream material descriptors because prepared_plant_material is the output entity. I also avoided capture/signal/derivative territory such as instrument settings, file formats, or analytical results. Since this is a researcher-operated process, I focused on collection protocol details, partitioning strategy, preservation/handling, and a small number of operational quality fields needed to reproduce the sampling step.

md_schema.descr: Method used to collect plant tissue for this workflow step, recorded at the time of sampling. Examples include 'leaf punch', 'stem excision', 'root excision', or 'whole tissue harvest'. This describes how material was obtained before any downstream extraction.

Plant tissue type collected during the sampling step, recorded immediately upon harvest. Use values such as leaf, stem, root, flower, seed, bark, or mixed_tissue to indicate the biological material entering downstream preparation.

How the collected plant tissue was divided for downstream genomic DNA extraction and metabolite analysis, recorded during sampling. For example, aliquoting into separate portions for DNA vs metabolite workflows, or splitting by tissue segment. This describes the process-level handling of the sample, not the resulting material identity.

Approximate mass of tissue collected per sample at the sampling point, in milligrams. Record the wet or fresh mass measured immediately after harvest, typically in the range of 1-5000 mg depending on plant size and workflow scale.

Type of container used to place the tissue immediately after collection, for example sterile tube, cryovial, foil packet, or collection bag. Record at sampling time because it influences preservation and traceability of the process.

Handling or preservation condition applied to tissue after collection and before downstream preparation, such as on_ice, flash_frozen, desiccated, or ambient_short_term. Record this immediately after sampling because it captures process handling that affects DNA and metabolite integrity.

Elapsed time in hours between tissue collection and transfer to downstream preparation or storage, measured at the sampling step. Typical values are 0-72 hours depending on transport and preservation; shorter times generally preserve nucleic acids and metabolites better.

Operational outcome flag indicating whether the collected tissue was suitable for downstream DNA extraction and metabolite analysis after sampling and partitioning. Record as a simple process-quality indicator at the end of the sampling step.

prepared_plant_material.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the prepared tissue state after sampling and before any extraction. I focused on what the material is now: its physical form, preservation status, storage conditions, and suitability for downstream DNA and metabolite extraction. I excluded sampling procedure details because those belong to the upstream plant_sampling process, and I excluded extraction reagents, timings, and outputs because those belong to downstream process nodes and their product entities. I also avoided repeating any identifiers already handled at the plant source or sampling stage unless they are needed to describe the prepared material itself.

md_schema.descr: Physical form of the collected plant tissue after preparation for downstream workflows, such as intact_tissue, chopped_tissue, ground_tissue, homogenized_tissue, or pooled_tissue. Record this as the state of the material immediately before DNA or metabolite extraction.

Current storage condition of the prepared plant material before extraction, for example frozen at -80 C, stored on dry ice, refrigerated at 4 C, or desiccated. This describes the material state at the time it is used for downstream extraction.

Elapsed time in hours that the prepared plant material has been held in its current storage condition before downstream extraction. Record at the point just before DNA or metabolite extraction; typical values range from 0 to several thousand hours depending on biobanking practice.

Qualitative or semi-quantitative assessment of tissue preservation after preparation, before extraction, typically reflecting visible degradation, thawing, or fragmentation. Record as a normalized score or lab-defined scale at the preparation stage to indicate suitability for downstream extraction.

Boolean indicator of whether a portion of the prepared plant material has been set aside specifically for downstream genomic DNA extraction. Record before extraction begins to describe the prepared material's allocation state.

Boolean indicator of whether a portion of the prepared plant material has been set aside specifically for downstream metabolite extraction. Record before extraction begins to describe the prepared material's allocation state.

Assessment of visible or documented contamination in the prepared material, such as soil, microbial growth, or cross-sample mix-up, determined before extraction. This is an entity-level suitability attribute for downstream processing.

dna_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only extraction protocol parameters, reagents, and a process-level quality outcome. I excluded properties of the prepared plant material because those belong to the upstream entity, and I excluded the extracted DNA product itself because that is the downstream plant_genomic_dna entity. I also excluded any sequencing or capture settings because those belong later in the workflow. Since the agent is researcher-operated, I focused on operational details that determine how genomic DNA was isolated and how successful the extraction was for sequencing use.

md_schema.descr: DNA isolation workflow used on the prepared plant material, recorded at the time of extraction. Examples include silica_column, magnetic_bead, phenol_chloroform, CTAB, or kit_based methods. This describes how genomic DNA was obtained, not the resulting DNA material.

Primary lysis buffer formulation used during genomic DNA extraction, described by the main chemical system or kit buffer name. Record at extraction time because it determines tissue disruption and nucleic acid release; if proprietary, use the kit or buffer identifier.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used for any digestion or lysis incubation during DNA extraction, measured as the protocol setpoint. Typical values are 20-70 C depending on method; record the controlled temperature at the extraction step.

Total incubation time in minutes used during the DNA extraction lysis or digestion phase, recorded as the protocol setpoint. Typical values range from a few minutes to several hours depending on method and tissue type.

Final volume of elution buffer or nuclease-free water used to recover genomic DNA from the purification matrix, in microliters. Record at the end of extraction because it defines the concentration and usability of the DNA product.

Total amount of genomic DNA recovered from the prepared plant material at the end of extraction, in nanograms. Typical yields range from low tens to many micrograms depending on tissue input and extraction efficiency.

Spectrophotometric A260/A280 purity ratio of the DNA extract measured after purification and before sequencing. Typical values near 1.8 indicate relatively pure DNA; record as a process quality indicator for extraction success.
Boolean indicator of whether the DNA extraction produced genomic DNA suitable for downstream genome sequencing. Record at the end of the process using the study's acceptance criteria.

plant_genomic_dna.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the extracted DNA material after the extraction process and before sequencing. I focused on identity, amount, purity, integrity, storage, and usability because these describe what the DNA is at the handoff to sequencing. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the upstream dna_extraction process, and I excluded sequencing instrument settings because those belong to the downstream genome_sequencing_capture node. I also avoided duplicate identifiers already handled at the plant source or process level.

md_schema.descr: Measured concentration of the extracted plant genomic DNA at the point of post-extraction QC, reported in nanograms per microliter. Typical values range from very low concentration to several hundred ng/ul depending on extraction yield and elution volume; record before sequencing library preparation.

Total recovered genomic DNA mass in nanograms for the extracted DNA sample, calculated or measured after extraction and before sequencing. This describes the amount of DNA available for library construction.

Quality score describing the integrity of the genomic DNA after extraction, assessed before sequencing using a lab-defined metric such as DIN, gel-based evaluation, or equivalent. Use a higher score to indicate more intact high-molecular-weight DNA.
Spectrophotometric A260/A280 ratio measured on the extracted genomic DNA prior to sequencing library preparation. Typical values near 1.8 indicate relatively protein-free DNA.
Spectrophotometric A260/A230 ratio measured on the extracted genomic DNA prior to sequencing library preparation. Typical values around 2.0-2.2 indicate low organic or salt contamination.

Buffer or solution in which the extracted genomic DNA is stored before sequencing, such as TE buffer, nuclease-free water, or low-EDTA buffer. Record this entity-level property at storage/transfer time because it affects DNA stability.

Storage temperature of the extracted genomic DNA before sequencing, in degrees Celsius. Common values are 4 C for short-term storage or -20 C / -80 C for longer-term storage; record at the time the DNA is held for downstream use.
Boolean indicator of whether the extracted genomic DNA passed QC and is suitable for genome sequencing input. Record at the handoff point to capture whether the entity meets downstream requirements.

genome_sequencing_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I included only the instrument configuration and measurement-session parameters for genome sequencing, along with the hardware agent description required for capture nodes. I excluded sample/DNA properties because those belong to the upstream plant_genomic_dna entity, and I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the downstream raw_genome_reads signal. I also avoided process/software fields because this is an instrument capture rather than a computational step. The selected fields are the minimum needed to understand and reproduce how the sequencing session was configured.

md_schema.descr: Manufacturer of the sequencing instrument used for this capture session, recorded as the hardware vendor at the time of genome sequencing. Example: 'Illumina' or 'Oxford Nanopore Technologies'. This is required on the Capture node because it describes the configured measurement apparatus.

Instrument model used for genome sequencing, recorded as the exact hardware model operating during the capture session. Example: 'NovaSeq 6000'. This specifies the measurement platform used to generate the raw sequencing reads.

Serial number or unique hardware identifier of the sequencing instrument used in this capture session, recorded at measurement time for traceability and reproducibility. Format is lab- or vendor-specific, for example 'NSQ-123456'.

Sequencing chemistry or reagent kit used on the instrument during the capture session, such as SBS kit version or flow-cell chemistry. Record at sequencing time because it defines how the DNA signal was acquired.

Configured read length in base pairs for the sequencing run, measured as the planned or achieved per-read length during capture. Typical values depend on platform and can range from 50 bp to several hundred bp or more.

Boolean indicator of whether the sequencing session was configured for paired-end read acquisition rather than single-end reading. Record during capture because it is an instrument/session setting that affects downstream raw reads.
Operational run mode of the sequencing instrument during the capture session, such as rapid, high_output, or standard. This describes how the instrument was configured for acquisition.

Identifier of the sequencing lane or flow cell used for this capture session, recorded during instrument operation for traceability. Use a string identifier such as a lane number or flow-cell barcode.
Date on which the genome sequencing capture session started, recorded at run initiation to mark the measurement session timing.
Boolean indicator of whether the sequencing capture session completed successfully enough to generate raw reads. Record at the end of the measurement session as a basic capture-quality flag.

raw_genome_reads.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I included only properties of the raw sequencing data artefact itself: file format, size, dimensions/volume of data, technical quality metrics, and storage location. I excluded capture settings and instrument details because those belong to the upstream genome_sequencing_capture node, and I excluded biological or computational interpretation because those belong downstream to assembly or analysis nodes. I also avoided duplicating any sequencing session identifiers already captured elsewhere, and kept the schema centered on what a downstream user needs to locate, inspect, and reuse the raw read files.

md_schema.descr: File format of the raw sequencing read artefact as stored after capture, recorded for the signal itself. Common values include FASTQ or BCL-derived exports; use the exact technical format used for downstream processing.

Total storage size of the raw genome read file set in bytes, measured for the signal artefact at the time of archival or transfer. This is a technical property of the data object, typically ranging from megabytes to terabytes depending on sequencing depth.
Total number of sequencing reads contained in the raw genome read artefact, counted after capture and before any trimming or filtering. This describes the data volume of the signal itself.

Total number of sequenced bases present in the raw genome read artefact, measured as the aggregate base count before downstream processing. Typical values depend on sequencing depth and platform and may range from millions to billions of bases.

Average raw per-base sequencing quality score for the read artefact, calculated across reads in the file set before trimming or correction. Record this as a technical quality metric for the signal, typically on the Phred scale.

Estimated percentage of reads or bases containing adapter contamination in the raw sequencing artefact, measured as a technical quality flag before processing. Typical values are low for clean libraries but can increase with short inserts or library artifacts.

Observed GC percentage across the raw read set, computed from the signal data before any assembly or filtering. This is a technical composition metric of the read artefact and is useful for QC and bias detection.

File system path, object-store URI, or repository location where the raw genome reads are stored, recorded for the signal artefact at archive or transfer time. Example formats include local paths, S3 URIs, or accession links.

MD5 checksum or equivalent file integrity hash for the raw genome read artefact, recorded at storage time to verify that the signal file has not been altered. Use a standard hex string such as 'd41d8cd98f00b204e9800998ecf8427e'.

genome_assembly_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only assembly protocol parameters, software/agent properties, and a process-level quality outcome. I excluded raw read file properties because those belong to the upstream raw_genome_reads signal, and I excluded assembled contig/scaffold properties because those belong to the downstream assembled_genome derivative. Since the agent is software, I followed the rule to describe software name, version, and repository on the Process node. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce how the reads were assembled and to judge whether the assembly succeeded.

md_schema.descr: Assembly software used for the genome assembly process, recorded as the exact program name running on the computational node. Example: 'SPAdes'. This belongs on the Process node because it describes the software agent performing the transformation.
Version of the genome assembly software used for this process step, recorded at runtime to ensure reproducibility. Example: '3.15.5'.

Repository, package source, or release location for the assembly software used in this process step, such as a GitHub URL, official download page, or package manager reference. Record this at the process stage to identify the exact implementation used.

Assembly strategy or algorithmic mode used to build contigs and scaffolds from raw reads, recorded during the assembly process. Examples include de_bruijn_graph, overlap_layout_consensus, or hybrid_assembly.

Set of k-mer sizes used by the assembly process, recorded as the parameter values supplied to the assembler. This is a process parameter relevant to read graph construction and should be captured at the time of assembly.

Minimum contig length in base pairs retained by the assembly process, recorded as a filtering or reporting threshold. Typical values are hundreds to thousands of base pairs and should be captured as a process setting.

Approximate sequencing depth of coverage provided to the assembly process, expressed as X-fold coverage and recorded for assembly interpretation. Typical values may range from low coverage to very high coverage depending on genome size and sequencing plan.

Boolean indicator of whether the genome assembly process completed successfully and produced an assembly suitable for downstream BGC analysis. Record this as a process-quality flag at the end of the assembly step.

assembled_genome.reasoning: I corrected the assembled_genome derivative schema by removing the colliding gc_percent field because it was already generated earlier in the DAG. I kept only assembly-specific computed output properties that remain within the derivative territory and do not duplicate upstream signal or process fields. The remaining fields still cover representation, contiguity, completeness, and usability of the assembled genome for downstream locus mapping and annotation.

md_schema.descr: File or sequence representation used for the assembled genome derivative, recorded as the final computational output format. Common examples include FASTA or GFA; record the format as stored for downstream locus mapping and annotation.

Number of contigs in the assembled genome, counted in the final assembly output after all filtering and scaffolding steps. This is a structural property of the derivative and is typically reported at assembly handoff.
Number of scaffolds in the assembled genome, counted in the final assembly output if scaffolding was performed. Record at the completed-assembly stage as a measure of assembly contiguity.

Total length of the assembled genome in base pairs, summed across all contigs or scaffolds in the final derivative. Typical values depend on plant genome size and should be recorded after assembly completion.
N50 statistic of the assembled genome in base pairs, calculated from the final contig or scaffold lengths. This is a standard assembly quality metric recorded for the computed genome derivative.
Length in base pairs of the largest contig in the assembly, recorded from the final assembled genome. This structural metric helps characterize assembly completeness and contiguity.

Quantitative estimate of assembly completeness recorded for the assembled genome derivative, typically based on a plant gene set benchmark such as BUSCO completeness or an equivalent metric. Record as a percentage or normalized score at the assembly output stage.
Boolean indicator of whether the assembled genome met the study's quality threshold for downstream locus mapping and gene annotation. Record at the derivative handoff as a usability flag.

bgc_identification_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I kept only fields that describe the BGC identification workflow itself and excluded any fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including software_name, software_version, and software_repository. I also excluded upstream assembled genome properties and downstream candidate BGC map properties because they belong to adjacent nodes. The schema therefore focuses on tool mode, detection thresholds, reference resources, and process-level output/quality indicators needed to reproduce and interpret the candidate cluster scan.

md_schema.descr: Identification mode used to scan the assembled genome for candidate biosynthetic gene clusters, recorded as the algorithmic or database-driven search setting. Examples include default, cluster_finder, or rule_based modes depending on the tool.

Minimum genomic span in base pairs required for a region to be reported as a candidate biosynthetic gene cluster, recorded as a process threshold during cluster identification. Typical values depend on the tool and organism and are set at analysis time.

Version or release date of the reference database, rule set, or biosynthetic motif library used during candidate BGC identification. Record this at the process stage because it directly affects which clusters are detected.
Number of candidate biosynthetic gene clusters reported by the identification process from the assembled genome, recorded as a process output summary at the end of the scan.

Overall confidence or score assigned by the BGC identification process to the reported candidate clusters, recorded as a process-level quality indicator. Use the tool's native score if available, or a normalized study-specific score.
Boolean indicator of whether the BGC identification step completed successfully and produced candidate cluster calls suitable for downstream locus mapping and gene annotation.

candidate_bgc_map.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed output properties of the candidate BGC map: its representation, locus count, locus coordinates/coverage, and derivative-level confidence or quality indicators. I excluded upstream assembled-genome or identification-process parameters because those belong to the preceding nodes, and I excluded downstream gene annotation details because those belong to the gene_annotation_process and annotated_bgc_table. I also avoided repeating software-related fields that were already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and focused on what a downstream user needs to inspect or reuse the locus map itself.

md_schema.descr: File or structured representation used for the candidate BGC map derivative, recorded as the final computational output format. Examples include GFF3, BED, TSV, or JSON depending on how loci are stored for downstream annotation.
Number of genomic loci reported in the candidate BGC map, counted in the final derivative after candidate cluster identification. This is a structural property of the computed map.

Genomic coordinates of candidate biosynthetic gene cluster loci represented in the map, stored as a standardized coordinate string or list structure in the derivative output. Use this to capture the position of each mapped locus on the assembled genome, for example contig name plus start-end intervals.
Total number of base pairs covered by all candidate biosynthetic gene cluster loci in the map, summed across mapped intervals. Record at the derivative stage as a measure of the mapped genomic span.

Mean confidence or scoring value assigned to candidate loci in the BGC map, computed from the underlying identification results and recorded as a derivative-level quality metric. Use the study's normalized score or the tool's native score if available.
Fraction of mapped candidate loci that meet the study's high-confidence threshold, computed from the final BGC map. Record as a value between 0 and 1 or as a percentage according to study convention.
Boolean indicator of whether the candidate BGC map met the study's quality threshold for downstream gene annotation. Record at the derivative handoff as a usability flag for this computed result.

gene_annotation_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only annotation workflow parameters, annotation reference details, and a process-level quality outcome for assigning predicted pathway function to genes within candidate BGC loci. I excluded the candidate locus coordinates because those belong to the upstream candidate_bgc_map derivative, and I excluded the annotated BGC table because that is the downstream output derivative. I also avoided software-name/version/repository fields that were already generated elsewhere in the DAG, to prevent collisions. The fields below capture the minimum process metadata needed to reproduce the gene annotation step and interpret its confidence.

md_schema.descr: Mode used to assign predicted pathway function to genes within candidate biosynthetic loci, recorded at the time of gene annotation. Examples include homology-based, motif-based, curated_rule_based, or combined annotation strategies.

Reference protein database, hidden Markov model library, or curated annotation set used to predict gene function within candidate BGC loci. Record the database name or release identifier at the annotation step because it governs the functional calls.
Version or release of the reference annotation database used during gene annotation, recorded for reproducibility. Example: '2024-01 release' or a specific database version string.
Threshold used by the annotation process to accept a gene-function assignment, such as percent identity, e-value, or score cutoff. Record the protocol- or tool-specific threshold at annotation time.
Number of genes within candidate biosynthetic loci that received predicted pathway-function annotations during this process step, recorded as an annotation summary at completion.

Fraction of genes in the candidate loci that were successfully assigned a predicted pathway function by the annotation process. Record as a value between 0 and 1 or as a percentage, depending on study convention.

Overall confidence level of the gene annotation process for the assigned pathway functions, recorded as a process-level quality indicator using the study's native scoring scheme or a normalized score.
Boolean indicator of whether the gene annotation step completed successfully and produced usable predicted pathway-function calls for downstream integration.

annotated_bgc_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only the computed table’s representation, contents, dimensions, and result-quality indicators. I excluded annotation software and thresholds because those belong to the upstream gene_annotation_process, and I excluded upstream locus map details because those belong to candidate_bgc_map. I also avoided repeating any software fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG. The selected fields are the minimum needed for a downstream user to interpret, filter, and reuse the annotated BGC table as a computed result.

md_schema.descr: Tabular representation used for the annotated BGC table derivative, recorded as the stored output format. Common examples include TSV, CSV, or Parquet; use the exact format in which the table is preserved for downstream analysis.
Number of rows in the annotated BGC table, counted in the final computed output. This is a structural property of the table derivative and indicates how many cluster-gene records are present.
Number of columns in the annotated BGC table, counted in the final computed output. This captures the dimensionality of the table at the derivative stage.
Number of distinct biosynthetic gene clusters represented in the annotated BGC table, counted after annotation and table assembly. This is a content summary for the computed result.
Number of gene-level annotation records contained in the table, counted across all cluster entries. This summarizes the amount of annotated pathway information captured in the derivative.

Fraction of genes or records in the table that have assigned predicted pathway function, calculated from the computed table contents. Record as a value between 0 and 1 or as a percentage according to study convention.
Boolean indicator of whether the annotated BGC table passed the study's completeness or export criteria for downstream integrative analysis. Record at the derivative handoff as a usability flag.

metabolite_extraction.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only extraction protocol parameters, solvent and cleanup details, and a process-level outcome for alkaloid enrichment. I excluded prepared material properties because those belong to the upstream entity, and I excluded the alkaloid extract’s composition or storage properties because those belong to the downstream entity. I also excluded profiling instrument settings and raw spectra file properties because those belong to the later capture and signal nodes. The selected fields are the minimum needed to reproduce how metabolites were extracted for chemical profiling and to assess extraction success.

md_schema.descr: Primary solvent or solvent mixture used to extract alkaloid-containing metabolites from prepared plant material, recorded at the time of extraction. Examples include methanol, ethanol, acetonitrile, or solvent mixtures with acid or water modifiers.

Ratio or composition of the extraction solvent mixture used in the metabolite extraction step, recorded as a protocol parameter. For example, methanol:water 80:20 or equivalent formulation used to enrich alkaloids.

Temperature in degrees Celsius used during metabolite extraction, measured as the protocol setpoint or maintained bath temperature. Typical values range from cold extraction at 4 C to heated extraction above room temperature.
Total duration in minutes of the metabolite extraction step, recorded as the protocol runtime from sample contact with solvent to completion of the extraction cycle.
Agitation or mixing mode used during metabolite extraction, recorded as a process parameter. Examples include vortexing, shaking, sonication, or incubation without agitation.

Post-extraction cleanup or concentration method applied to the metabolite extract before chemical profiling, recorded as part of the extraction workflow. Examples include SPE, filtration, evaporation, or dilution.
Amount of crude metabolite extract recovered at the end of the extraction process, in milligrams. Typical yields depend on tissue input and solvent system and are recorded as a process outcome.

Boolean indicator of whether the extraction protocol was intended to enrich alkaloids specifically rather than capture a broad metabolite fraction. Record at the end of the process to describe the extraction objective and outcome.

alkaloid_extract.reasoning: This node is an Entity, so I included only intrinsic properties of the alkaloid extract after extraction and before mass spectrometry. I focused on composition, concentration, volume, storage, and enrichment/suitability because these describe what the extract is as a material. I excluded extraction protocol details because those belong to the upstream metabolite_extraction process, and I excluded profiling instrument settings and spectra because those belong to the downstream capture and signal nodes. I also avoided introducing any fields that would duplicate identifiers or process outcomes already captured elsewhere.

md_schema.descr: Material class of the extract at the entity stage, recorded as an alkaloid-enriched crude extract or a fractionated extract. Use this to distinguish the extract from the original tissue and from analytical outputs.

Measured volume of the alkaloid extract available for downstream profiling, in microliters. Record this at the point the extract is handed off to chemical characterization; typical volumes depend on sample scale and concentration.

Concentration of dissolved extract material in milligrams per milliliter, measured after extraction and before mass spectrometry. Typical values vary widely with tissue input and solvent evaporation; record as an entity property of the extract solution.

Main alkaloid class expected or enriched in the extract, based on prior extraction knowledge or preliminary composition assessment. Examples include indole, isoquinoline, tropane, quinolizidine, or steroidal alkaloids.
Storage temperature of the alkaloid extract before chemical profiling, in degrees Celsius. Common values include 4 C, -20 C, or -80 C depending on anticipated storage duration.

Solvent used to store or reconstitute the alkaloid extract before profiling, for example methanol, acetonitrile, water, or acidified solvent mixtures. Record the storage medium as an entity property because it affects stability and injection readiness.
Boolean indicator of whether the alkaloid extract was judged ready for mass spectrometry profiling based on clarity, concentration, and absence of visible particulates or precipitation.

Qualitative assessment of the extract's compositional cleanliness before profiling, such as clean, minor_impurities, or mixed_fraction. Record this as an entity-level suitability attribute for downstream chemical analysis.

alkaloid_profiling_capture.reasoning: This node is a Capture, so I kept only mass spectrometry session settings and outcomes, while removing the repeated hardware identity fields that collided with earlier capture steps in the DAG. I excluded alkaloid extract properties because those belong to the upstream entity, and I excluded raw spectra file metadata because that belongs to the downstream signal. The remaining fields describe how the profiling measurement was configured and whether it produced usable spectra, which is the correct semantic territory for this capture node.

md_schema.descr: Ionization polarity or mode configured for the alkaloid profiling session, recorded at measurement time. Common values include positive and negative ionization, which affect which alkaloid species are detected.

Mass analyzer type used during the capture session, such as Orbitrap, time-of-flight, quadrupole, or ion trap. Record this instrument configuration because it determines the raw chemical spectra acquired.

Configured mass-to-charge scan range in m/z units for the profiling session, recorded as the acquisition window used to generate raw spectra. Typical ranges depend on alkaloid size and instrument settings.
Fragmentation or MS/MS acquisition mode used during profiling, such as CID, HCD, or no fragmentation. Record at capture time because it defines how the spectra were acquired.
Volume of alkaloid extract injected into the mass spectrometer for this capture session, in microliters. Record at measurement time because it directly affects signal intensity and spectra quality.
Total duration of the mass spectrometry profiling capture session in minutes, measured from the start to the end of the run. Typical values depend on method length and number of scans acquired.
Date on which the mass spectrometry profiling capture session was performed, recorded at run initiation for session traceability.
Boolean indicator of whether the profiling capture session completed successfully and generated usable raw chemical spectra. Record at the end of the measurement session as a capture-quality flag.

raw_chemical_spectra.reasoning: This node is a Signal, so I kept only raw spectra file properties that do not collide with fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG. I excluded file_format, file_size_bytes, storage_uri, and checksum_md5 because those were already produced on previous signal nodes. I also excluded capture settings and chemical interpretation because those belong upstream and downstream, respectively. The remaining fields describe the raw chemical spectra artefact itself in terms of technical dimensions and QC, which is the correct semantic territory for a signal node.

md_schema.descr: Total number of spectra contained in the raw chemical spectra artefact, counted after acquisition and before any peak picking or filtering. This describes the data volume of the signal itself.

Total number of mass spectrometry scans represented in the raw spectra artefact, counted before downstream processing. This is a technical dimension of the signal file and reflects acquisition length.

Lower bound of the recorded mass-to-charge range in the raw spectra artefact, expressed in m/z units. Record this from the signal metadata to characterize the measured window before any annotation or filtering.

Upper bound of the recorded mass-to-charge range in the raw spectra artefact, expressed in m/z units. Record this from the signal metadata to characterize the measured window before any annotation or filtering.
Average signal-to-noise ratio across the raw chemical spectra, calculated as a technical quality metric before any peak annotation or normalization. Higher values generally indicate cleaner spectra.

Estimated baseline noise level in the raw spectra artefact, measured before downstream processing and reported using the instrument or pipeline's native scale. This is a technical quality metric for the signal file.
Number of precursor ions represented in the raw chemical spectra, counted from the unprocessed data before annotation or feature extraction. This is a technical property of the signal artefact.

Total ion current integrated across the raw chemical spectra, recorded as a technical intensity summary of the signal before downstream processing. Typical values depend on instrument sensitivity and sample abundance.
Boolean indicator of whether the raw chemical spectra passed the study's minimum technical quality threshold for downstream peak detection and annotation. Record as a signal-level usability flag.

alkaloid_annotation_process.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I kept only computational parameters and quality indicators specific to alkaloid spectral interpretation, while avoiding duplicate field ids already used elsewhere in the DAG. I excluded raw spectra file properties because those belong to the upstream signal, and I excluded the characterized alkaloid products because those belong to the downstream derivative. Since annotation_coverage_fraction was already generated in an earlier step, I replaced it with a different process-level summary field that still captures interpretation yield without colliding with prior metadata. The schema below remains within the process territory and is sufficient for reproducibility and interpretation of the annotation step.

md_schema.descr: Method used to deconvolute overlapping ions or fragments before alkaloid identification, recorded during the annotation process. Examples include centroiding, peak_picking, de_isotoping, or no_deconvolution depending on the workflow.
Minimum spectral matching score required for accepting an alkaloid annotation, recorded as a process parameter at annotation time. Use the study's native score cutoff or library-specific threshold.

Estimated false discovery rate in percent associated with the alkaloid annotation calls, calculated or specified by the pipeline at the end of the process. This is a process-level quality indicator for annotation reliability.

Boolean indicator of whether manual expert review or curation was applied to the automatically generated alkaloid annotations. Record at the end of the process to indicate whether computational calls were inspected or adjusted.

Number of spectral features or peaks assigned an alkaloid annotation during this process step, recorded as a summary output at completion. This describes the yield of interpreted features without duplicating prior coverage fields.

Typical retention-time deviation in seconds between observed spectra and the top reference hit used during annotation, recorded as a process diagnostic. This is useful when chromatographic alignment contributes to compound identification.

Boolean flag indicating whether the alkaloid annotation process passed the study's acceptance criteria after any filtering or curation steps. Record this at process completion as the final usability indicator.

characterized_alkaloids.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only computed output properties of the characterized alkaloid list: its table/list representation, counts, content dimensions, and result-quality indicators. I excluded annotation process parameters because those belong upstream to alkaloid_annotation_process, and I excluded raw spectra properties because those belong upstream to raw_chemical_spectra. I also avoided field ids already generated elsewhere in the DAG, including annotation_coverage_fraction. The selected fields are the minimum needed to interpret and reuse the characterized compound set as a computed result.

md_schema.descr: Structured representation used for the characterized alkaloids derivative, recorded as the final stored output format. Common examples include CSV, TSV, JSON, or a database table depending on how compound features are preserved for downstream analysis.
Number of chemically characterized alkaloid compounds reported in the final derivative, counted after annotation and curation. This is a structural summary of the computed result.

Number of distinct chemical features or compound-feature records contained in the characterized alkaloids output, counted after computational interpretation. This summarizes the dimensionality of the derivative.
Number of distinct alkaloid classes represented among the characterized compounds, counted from the final interpreted output. This helps summarize chemical diversity in the derivative.

Mean confidence or spectral matching score across characterized alkaloid calls, computed from the final derivative and recorded as a result-quality metric. Use the study's native score scale or normalized equivalent.

Fraction of characterized alkaloid calls that meet the study's high-confidence threshold, computed from the final output. Record as a value between 0 and 1 or as a percentage according to study convention.
Boolean indicator of whether the characterized alkaloid list passed the study's final curation or validation criteria for downstream integrative analysis.

integrative_pathway_analysis.reasoning: This node is a Process, so I included only integrative-analysis parameters, linkage criteria, and a process-level output quality indicator. I excluded upstream genomic and chemical result fields because those belong to the annotated_bgc_table and characterized_alkaloids derivatives, and I excluded the final integrated result table because that belongs to the downstream pathway_insight_table derivative. I also avoided any software-name/version/repository fields already generated elsewhere in the DAG, and kept the schema focused on how the integration was performed and judged rather than on the upstream source data.

md_schema.descr: Strategy used to jointly analyze annotated biosynthetic gene clusters and characterized alkaloids, recorded at the time of integrative analysis. Examples include correlation_based, rule_based_mapping, network_based_linking, or expert_curated integration.

Primary criterion used to link biosynthetic genes or clusters with alkaloid products, recorded as the analysis rule or threshold applied during integration. Examples include co-occurrence, genomic proximity, pathway homology, shared module membership, or spectral similarity.

Minimum score or similarity threshold required to accept a gene-cluster-to-compound link during the integrative analysis, recorded as the process cutoff. Use the study's native scoring scheme or a normalized threshold value.

Number of nodes used in the integrative analysis graph or linkage network, counted at the end of the process. This may include clusters, genes, compounds, or features depending on the integration design.
Number of links or edges evaluated or retained in the integrative analysis graph, counted at process completion. This is a structural summary of the integration step.
Number of gene-cluster-to-alkaloid links that passed the study's acceptance criteria during integrative analysis, recorded as a process outcome summary.

Overall confidence score for the integrative pathway analysis, recorded as a process-level quality indicator summarizing the strength of the gene-to-alkaloid links. Use the study's native score or a normalized equivalent.
Boolean indicator of whether the integrative analysis completed successfully and produced usable pathway links for the final insight table.

pathway_insight_table.reasoning: This node is a Derivative, so I included only the computed integrated result properties: the table representation, dimensionality, linkage counts, and result-quality indicators. I excluded the upstream genomic and chemical inputs because those belong to annotated_bgc_table and characterized_alkaloids, and I excluded the integration strategy parameters because those belong to integrative_pathway_analysis. I also avoided any previously generated field ids and kept the schema focused on what a downstream user needs to understand and reuse the final pathway insight output.

md_schema.descr: Structured representation used for the pathway insight derivative, recorded as the final stored output format. Common examples include TSV, CSV, JSON, or Parquet depending on how the integrated result is preserved for downstream use.
Number of rows in the final pathway insight table, counted after integration. This is a structural property of the computed result and reflects the number of pathway-link records.
Number of columns in the pathway insight table, counted in the final derivative. This summarizes the dimensionality of the integrated result.
Number of distinct biosynthetic gene clusters represented in the final integrative result, counted after pathway analysis. This is a content summary of the derivative.
Number of distinct characterized alkaloids represented in the final integrative result, counted after pathway analysis. This summarizes how many chemical products are linked in the derivative.
Number of gene-cluster-to-alkaloid pathway links reported in the final insight table, counted after integration. This is the key output size metric for the derivative.

Overall confidence score for the final pathway insights, computed from the integrated gene-cluster and alkaloid evidence and recorded as a derivative-level quality indicator. Use the study's native score or a normalized equivalent.

Boolean indicator of whether the final pathway insight table met the study's acceptance criteria for downstream interpretation or publication. Record at the derivative handoff as the final usability flag.
